topics.label: Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, recaps the previous histopathology practicals, and outlines the main learning outcomes of the lecture.

topics.label: Tumor Viruses, Proto-Oncogenes, and Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed that cancer originates from altered cellular genes, and describe the experimental assays used to test transforming capacity in vitro and in vivo.

topics.label: Classes, Mechanisms, and Mutational Dynamics of Cancer Genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the operational definitions of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes, their roles in regulating the cell cycle checkpoint, and the functional consequences of dominant, recessive, and dominant-negative mutations.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Consequences of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how failures in distinct DNA repair pathways, replication machinery, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-Step Tumor Progression, Hereditary Predisposition, and Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the stepwise accumulation of mutations during tumorigenesis, the accelerated tumor development seen in hereditary cancer syndromes, and how genetic instability influences tumor evolution.

topics.label: Conclusion, Reading Recommendations, and Next Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, suggests supplementary reading, and notes the topic for the following lecture.
